fieldValues.title: Escalation: what naming rule do Type and Vocabulary names follow? (srs#236)
fieldValues.decision_question: Should the SRS standard require snake_case for Type and Vocabulary names, as its text says, or keep the kebab-case that every existing Type and Vocabulary already uses?
fieldValues.context: Problem: The standard says Field and Type names are snake_case, but 151 of the live Type, View, Composition, Blueprint and Vocabulary names (including the standard's own self-description) are kebab-case. A builder tried to turn the rule into an enforced check (srs#236, P0, blocks the gate) and found the check would fail on all of them, because Fields, Types and Vocabularies share one `name` Field. The safe half (the `namespace` rule, 0 violations) is already going ahead. Why it matters: the written rule and the practice disagree, and whichever is chosen becomes what third parties are told to follow; it is a change to the written standard, which is yours to make, not the group's. Options and consequences: (1) Rename all 151 names: the text stays true, but the change reaches the metamodel generator, every rendered spec page and every reference by name, so it is large and risky for no visible gain. (2) Keep Field names snake_case and write Type and Vocabulary names as kebab-case in the standard: matches what everyone already does, small change, but it needs two separate `name` Fields so the checks can differ, and a spec text edit. (3) Grandfather the 151 and enforce snake_case only for new names: no rewrite, but the rule stays half-enforced and surprising. Recommendation: option 2. Action needed: decide. Urgency: medium; srs#236 is labelled blocks-gate and waits until this is settled. Answers: no affirmed problem yet (the standard's naming rule disagrees with its own corpus). Detail: https://github.com/the-greenman/srs/issues/236 (audit and options in the last comment).
fieldValues.friction: The written rule and the corpus disagree, so a check cannot be turned on without either rewriting the corpus or changing the rule, and only the owner can change the standard's written rules.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: 1. Rename all 151 Type and Vocabulary names to snake_case. 2. Split the convention by kind: Field names snake_case, Type and Vocabulary names kebab-case (recommended). 3. Grandfather existing names and enforce only for new ones.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Recommended: Field names stay snake_case; Type and Vocabulary names are documented as kebab-case, matching the corpus; the shared `name` Field is split so each kind can carry its own pattern. This is a proposal for the owner to decide.
fieldValues.rationale: Nothing is broken today by kebab-case Type names (no ambiguity or parsing failure), and renaming 151 definitions risks the metamodel, rendered specs and by-name references for no gain. Aligning the text with practice is the smallest honest change.
fieldValues.revisit_when: After the split is in place and one full release has run the new checks without a corpus failure.
fieldValues.next_steps: Owner decides. If option 2: a Door 2 spec text edit (docs/spec/srs-spec.md line 196) and a follow-up issue to split the Field; the namespace pattern PR for srs#236 proceeds independently.
